record.context_brief: Translate finite-power closure to stronger Borel properties
record.original_question: If a space X satisfies S_1(B_Ω, B_Ω), must every finite power of X satisfy S_1(B, B)? And if X satisfies S_fin(B_Ω, B_Ω), must every finite power of X satisfy S_1(B_Γ, B)?

evidence.quote: Problem 8.3 ([47, Problems 19 and 21]). (1) Is it true that if X satisfies S1(BΩ, BΩ), then all finite powers of X satisfy S1(B, B)? (2) Is it true that if X satisfies Sfin(BΩ, BΩ), then all finite powers of X satisfy S1(BΓ, B)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a topological space (typically a set of real numbers or a separable metric space). For a family A of countable covers of X, recall the following standard selection principles:
- S_1(A, B): for every sequence (U_n)_{n∈ω} with U_n ∈ A there exist U_n ∈ U_n such that {U_n : n ∈ ω} ∈ B.
- S_fin(A, B): for every sequence (U_n)_{n∈ω} with U_n ∈ A there exist finite F_n ⊆ U_n such that ⋃_n F_n ∈ B.

A countable cover U of X (consisting of proper subsets) is called:
- a Borel cover (notation B) if every element of U is a Borel subset of X;
- a Borel ω-cover (notation B_Ω) if every finite subset of X is contained in some single element of U;
- a Borel γ-cover (notation B_Γ) if U is infinite and every point of X belongs to all but finitely many elements of U.

The classes B, B_Ω, B_Γ are the Borel analogues of the classical classes of open covers, ω-covers, and γ-covers.

Answer the following two questions:

(1) If X satisfies S_1(B_Ω, B_Ω), does every finite power X^n (n ≥ 1) satisfy S_1(B, B)?

(2) If X satisfies S_fin(B_Ω, B_Ω), does every finite power X^n (n ≥ 1) satisfy S_1(B_Γ, B)?
artifact.status_search_result: Survey literature on selection principles (e.g., works by Scheepers, Tsaban and collaborators on Borel-cover analogues of the Scheepers diagram and surveys of open problems) lists preservation of selection properties under finite powers among the central open problems. No source located resolves these two specific implications for Borel ω-covers, so the status appears to remain open, but this could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: Selection principles in mathematics: A milestone of open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Tsaban and colleagues extended studies of selection principles for families of open covers of sets of real numbers to also include families of countable Borel covers.
status_evidence.claim: The Borel-cover versions of the selection principles and their finite-power behavior are a standard topic with several open problems listed in surveys.

status_evidence.title: Selection principles and proofs from the Book
status_evidence.snippet: Open problem asks whether properties such as S_1 and S_fin over Borel/ω-classes are preserved under finite powers.
status_evidence.claim: Preservation under finite powers for these Borel selection classes is recognized as an open problem in recent surveys.
